comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
It's a lot clearer now.

Most of the shit I've gotten over the years has nothing to do with what I've been saying and everything to do with the fact that many people get offended by what they perceive as audaciousness. They wouldn't dare bring up topics, ask questions, or make assertions the way I do for fear they'd be taken as total A-holes. So, they automatically peg me for an A-hole putting them on the spot, completely zone out about what I said, and attack me personally -- some less flagrantly than others.

So, I'm taken for a "troll". OK. If outing posers and liars and airheads and bloviating fools is "trolling", I'm guilty, gladly.

Honest people don't take me that way.

As soon as I'm satisfied that I can shut fools down and make them painfully obvious, I might switch my approach. I don't like talking with people like that, anyway. But as long as people defend and fight to protect their follies, especially when they're more than willing to hurt and harm people in the process, I'll probably keep it up.

Too bad they'll never get to see that I don't behave in any way remotely like that when I'm talking with honest people who want the truth just like I do.

Egos can just go fuck off and die. I've got no respect for them, because they deserve none, mine included.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
Of course it is. 

The more fundamental problem has nothing to do with individualism or interdependence, and everything to do with the premise for "freedom".

As we typically conceive it, "freedom" is a function of absence of adversity. In other words: if no one stops us from doing what we want to do, we’re “free”.

Bullshit. That’s not nearly what real freedom is.

It’s a very typical notion, though, one that conforms to the way both children and psychopaths see the world.

Compare that notion of freedom to this one:

We’re free when we can be honest, be genuinely ourselves, and be accepted as we are for who we are without anyone trying to stop us or deny us or diss us or defame us.

Which version involves a deeper, far more powerful kind of freedom?

This kind of freedom takes interdependence to a whole new level, doesn’t it?

Why don’t we have that in mind when we think and talk about freedom?

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
I appreciate your intent and am down 100% with the fact that what is, is now, that's all there is, so that's all the truth could be about. It's kinda like the extremely honest person who couldn't tell you the time because by the time they'd looked up from their watch to open their mouth, the second hand had already moved.

The "just be" sentiment -- to the point it's a denial of sense-making -- is just not enough, though. Your post is the result of sense-making which involved ruminating both about the now, the "past", and potential "futures". It feels much better to experience just being in the now, but you'd have a hard time arguing that such experience is sufficient for us to proceed intelligently and successfully through life, or that our "obsession" with sense-making is pathological. But maybe I'm oversimplifying what you're saying here?

comment.body:
Well worth your time. I watched the one on the Zapatistas (#4). I'd really like to go live with them awhile.

My message here is that you and I have had near-zero awareness how prevalent "horizontal" movements have been historically, and ne'er a fucking clue how prevalent they are right now all around the world.

The "Utopian", "pie-in-the-sky", and "idealistic" ideas and practices that you think are completely unrealistic, naive, and impractical have already been done for thousands of years and are already being done by hundreds of millions around the world.

You know why you think "that will never happen"? Because that utterly superstitious belief is necessary to keep you imprisoned in these concentration camps we call "nations" while you, the whole time, delude yourself and gloat about your "freedom".

People regularly dared me to "prove" that what I'm talking about is true and doable. I never really did, because if they need me to shove their heads into the water I led them to, they can damn-well just dehydrate where they stand, lol.

Besides, as I see more clearly every day, it was proven ages ago (literally). Our current insane OCD insistence on authoritarianism is less than 15,000 years old. It's a delusion. In fact, it's a mental illness. "Civilization" refers to nothing more than massive extortion cults. Outside of that, human beings have been fairly sane. And many of us still are or, like me, have come back to their senses. I can't say how sane I am at the moment, but I know it's more than yesterday, and will be more tomorrow, cuz I refuse to in any other direction.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eKaFf1OnQ0o

comment.name: Roman Bystrianyk
comment.body:
It seems to us today that toxic medications are being pushed all over the place for treating conditions that are best addressed by nutritional deficiencies or lifestyle modification (e.g., getting exercise and sunshine.) Would you be surprised that medical men have been doing this for centuries?

“Mankind has been drugged to death, and the world would be better off if the contents of every apothecary shop were emptied into the sea, though the consequences to the fishes would be lamentable. The disgrace of medicine has been that colossal system of self-deception, in obedience to which mines have been emptied of their cankering minerals, the entrails of animals taxed for their impurities, the poison-bags of reptiles drained of their venom and all the inconceivable abominations thus obtained thrust down the throats of human beings suffering from some fault of organization, nourishment or vital stimulation.” ― Dr. Oliver Wendell Holmes, 1860s

[“Honest Confessions of Weakness,” Journal of Osteopathy, vol. IV, no. 5, October 1897, Kirksville, Missouri, p. 228.]
